text: Human expertise is often built. <break time="0.8s" /> On a complex web of implicit knowledge. <break time="0.8s" /> That we acquire with practice over time. <break time="0.8s" /> What we call experience in our job resumes. <break time="0.8s" /> That is true of every profession. <break time="0.8s" /> From architects and hairdressers. <break time="0.8s" /> To musicians, leadership coaches, sales staff. <break time="0.8s" /> And law enforcement personnel. <break time="0.8s" /> Data driven machine learning. <break time="0.8s" /> Offers a tantalizing opportunity. <break time="0.8s" /> To capture this kind of implicit knowledge. <break time="0.8s" /> And operationalize it for better decision making. <break time="0.8s" /> Generative AI models. <break time="0.8s" /> Are an excellent case in point. <break time="0.8s" /> By being trained. <break time="0.8s" /> On half a trillion words of training text. <break time="0.8s" /> Including everything from books and manuals to Wikipedia. <break time="0.8s" /> They ingested. <break time="0.8s" /> A wealth of knowledge about the world. <break time="0.8s" /> Without such knowledge being expressed in obvious rules. <break time="0.8s" /> As an analogy. <break time="0.8s" /> Think of cooking. <break time="0.8s" /> Recipes may offer. <break time="0.8s" /> A step by step way to prepare a meal. <break time="0.8s" /> But almost all of them leave out certain steps. <break time="0.8s" /> That their authors considered obvious, trivial. <break time="0.8s" /> Or perhaps too subtle to mention. <break time="0.8s" /> But when one carefully reads between the lines of many of them. <break time="0.8s" /> The implicit knowledge can be accessed. <break time="0.8s" /> That is how generative AI works as well. <break time="0.8s" /> And why it is a step change from what came before it.
